verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a TLD price-list endpoint that returns an alphabetical list of every supported TLD with pricing for each order type. It also exposes Retail (Public Site) Pricing alongside account-level and original pricing, and links to a public pricing page. That covers a published per-TLD price list with separate order-type prices. Nothing in the evidence shows whether first-year prices match renewal prices, so the 'no teaser price hiding a renewal spike' part of the story cannot be confirmed. Missing for 10: evidence that first-year and renewal prices match (or that renewal spikes are disclosed), an explicit breakdown of registration, renewal and transfer columns on the public pricing page, and independent or hands-on confirmation of pricing transparency.
